mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based demand contraction. This combination reduces corporate sales and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such joint-triggered episodes, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 in a single month, combined with an unemployment rate below 4%, signals an overheating labor market. This combination increases wage inflation and cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such triggered episodes, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 0.5% for more than one year during a period of positive GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an extended accommodative monetary policy stance. This supports corporate borrowing and investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% for >12 months AND GDPC1 positive trend
regime_hint: prolonged monetary easing with economic expansion
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of such triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, indicating weakening consumer demand. This mechanism predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 5% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such triggered episodes, or the joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).
